scope: Replacement reference covering all historical Massassi flag/value table families, plus related domains. All32 ThingFlags positions accounted for; not every per-bit meaning or retail target is proven.

evidence_policy.declaration-only: Source symbol and numeric identity; no inspected per-bit consumer promised.
evidence_policy.bounded-source-analysis: Named readers/writers in selected source; not original retail execution.
evidence_policy.unresolved-consumer: No meaning established by the bounded investigation. Not safe spare state.
evidence_policy.source-consumer: Specific inspected source consumer; target caveats apply.
evidence_policy.original-retail-static: Selected byte-verified original JK1.01/MotS code paths, including the separately described ThingFlags wrapper/queue/serializer contract and explicitly marked 0.1.5 per-value findings. Not a runtime test or proof of every consumer.
evidence_policy.target_separation: Pinned enhanced snapshot, current local source, original JK, original MotS, and Indy reconstruction remain distinct.
evidence_policy.unresolved-name: Numeric or explicitly unknown declaration label. No meaning is certified by the name; dedicated consumers may still exist.
evidence_policy.current-source-consumer: Individually hashed current enhanced-source reader/writer; original-game meaning remains unestablished unless separately stated.
evidence_policy.original-retail-cog-source: Complete hash-identified original COG and relevant bindings inspected; source contract is distinct from runtime execution and native-engine consumers.
evidence_policy.original-retail-runtime-wine: Unchanged hash-identified original executable actually run under the stated Wine/Xvfb fixture; results apply only to tested contexts and observation limits.

families.title: Thing flags
families.notes: Every 32-bit position is catalogued. Semantic evidence is bounded and target-specific.

entries.description: ThingLight nonzero immediate branch enables the bit; template light= also enables it. Current renderer uses it with positive light and excludes disabled/hidden/destroyed things in the inspected light-collection path.
entries.caveat: A bit alone supplies neither positive intensity nor a model. Zero immediate ThingLight updates intensity but does not clear the bit.

entries.description: Marks pending removal: ordinary update takes the RemoveThing branch when set; DestroyThing sets it and conditionally sends removed.
entries.caveat: Setting the bit directly bypasses DestroyThing’s immediate removed-notification step. Clearing it is not resurrection or recreation.

entries.description: Participates in a projectile deflection/ricochet branch when the colliding weapon has SITH_WF_IMPACTSOUND; successful collision handling reflects velocity, changes orientation and plays deflected sound.
entries.caveat: Not a demonstrated universal invulnerability switch. Conditions include weapon flags, bounce limits and collision handler success; other damage routes are separate.

entries.description: Separates model things into the level-geometry rendering pass; the ordinary thing pass excludes them.
entries.caveat: Does not by itself make physics immobile, create collision geometry or ensure a model exists.

entries.description: Filters a thing out of inspected geometry/ordinary rendering and light-collection paths.
entries.caveat: Describe as render-hidden in these paths, not global disabled: no claim that scripts, physics, collision or sound stop.

entries.description: No symbolic consumer found in the bounded reviewed runtime files; remains a numeric enum entry.
entries.caveat: This is not proof that the bit is unused, safe as user storage, absent in retail, or never set in historical COGs.
entries.anchors: P: types_enums.h:1329; bounded search scope below.

entries.description: A RAYCAST_10 collision search only accepts candidate things carrying this bit. Pinned floor-finding chooses that mode for non-wall-stick downward search.
entries.caveat: Still requires ordinary collision eligibility; does not create collision geometry, an actor attachment or a valid floor automatically.
entries.behavior_evidence: Pinned query caller plus current collision consumer

entries.description: When searchFlags includes RAYCAST_8, only thing candidates with this bit pass that filter. Current CheckPathClear issues 0x12A, which includes8.
entries.caveat: Use this exact query-filter meaning; do not call it universal collidable, LOS-blocking or ignored-by-all-physics. Other query modes and candidate checks differ.

entries.description: Suppresses selected COG notifications such as damaged/removed/sector exited. Pinned multiplayer setup marks non-server non-actor things with it. Current actor damage branch bypasses health subtraction when multiplayer and this flag is set.
entries.caveat: Not the separate actor SITH_AF_INVULNERABLE bit. The inspected single-player actor path does not make this thing flag a universal damage shield; suppressing damaged notification can also bypass a script’s damage adjustment.
entries.behavior_evidence: Pinned message gates; current actor damage consumer

entries.description: DamageThing rejects dead things. Current DestroyActor sets DEAD while converting the thing to corpse and changing physics/lifetime; current KillActor returns early when already dead.
entries.caveat: DEAD is distinct from DESTROYED. Setting it alone does not perform the complete killed/corpse sequence or schedule removal.
entries.behavior_evidence: Pinned damage consumer; current actor writer

entries.description: CaptureThing sets capture pointer plus bit; template class COG binding and linked COG references also set it. Several engine notifications test it.
entries.caveat: Setting the bit alone installs no COG pointer or link. ReleaseThing clears the bit only if no class COG or surviving thing link requires it.

entries.description: Suppresses two explicit crush/impact-damage calls generated when a moving/pushing thing cannot move its attached passenger or collided target far enough. The tested flag is on the mover/pusher.
entries.caveat: Do not document as blanket fall/impact immunity on the victim. Ordinary collision movement/blocking remains, and unrelated damage paths are not covered.

entries.description: Loading computes 0x1000 << jkPlayer_setDiff and frees an explicit level thing when its flags intersect that exclusion mask; this is bit 0x1000 for difficulty index 0.
entries.caveat: Identified consumer is a load-time exclusion; runtime SetThingFlags does not rerun the loader. Easy label comes from enum.

entries.description: Same load-time mask, bit 0x2000 for difficulty index 1.
entries.caveat: Do not present as a continuously enforced runtime hide/disable switch.

entries.description: Same load-time mask, bit 0x4000 for difficulty index 2.
entries.caveat: Do not present as a continuously enforced runtime hide/disable switch.

entries.description: The loader includes 0x8000 in its exclusion mask when g_submodeFlags bit 1 is set. Multiplayer startup sets that submode bit, supporting a multiplayer-exclusion label for this path.
entries.caveat: Template/placement/load-time behavior, not a general runtime multiplayer-locality flag. Do not confuse with COG execution or transport flags.

entries.description: The loader adds this bit to its rejection mask when submode bit 1 is clear. A populated level thing whose flags intersect that mask is freed. The corresponding multiplayer branch adds 0x8000 instead. Source multiplayer startup sets the submode bit, supporting the shorthand single-player placement exclusion.
entries.caveat: This is a loading condition. Setting it after loading does not by itself hide or destroy the thing. The precise original predicate is submode bit 1 clear; other rejection bits, including difficulty, still apply.

prior_interpretation_0_1_4.caveat: Do not label unused or import another game's meaning. Literal/composite masks, other repositories/builds, and original binaries were not exhausted.

entries.description: **Engine-maintained thing pulse state.** P Cog/sithCogFunctionThing.c:598–617: SetThingPulse sets bit plus interval/next time, or clears all three for exactly zero. P Cog/sithCog.c:1544–1550: due pulse advances next time and sends the thing PULSE message.
entries.caveat: P World/sithThing.c:236–240 skips this processing while DISABLED. OR-ing the bit alone does not initialize the interval/deadline. This is the thing timer facility, not the COG instance's SetPulse state.

entries.description: **Engine-maintained one-shot thing timer state.** P Cog/sithCogFunctionThing.c:619–636: SetThingTimer writes deadline/bit, or clears both for exactly zero. P Cog/sithCog.c:1551–1554 clears the bit before sending TIMER when due.
entries.caveat: Disabled things skip the update. Setting the flag alone does not establish a meaningful deadline. Both thing timer wrappers are registered outside the nearby MotS branch at P Cog/sithCogFunctionThing.c:2714–2723; this is source registration evidence, not retail proof.

entries.description: **Broad disable state/configuration, not just invisibility.** P World/sithThing.c:224–240 still handles lifetime before skipping subsequent timer/control/type updates; :470–477 rejects incoming damage and :732–733/:809–812 suppress sector notifications. C Engine/sithRender.c:2770–2772 excludes disabled ordinary things; C Engine/sithCollision.c:246–250 excludes them from the shown collision-candidate path.
entries.caveat: Lifetime/respawn work is not universally frozen. Dedicated C writers: World/sithItem.c:60–87 sets while awaiting respawn, :116–129 clears on respawn; Gameplay/sithPlayer.c:29–45 sets during slot startup, :471–483 clears when showing player. C Dss/sithDSSThing.c:244–259 has a MotS-specific disabled-to-enabled item/MP/client/respawn-factor/respawn-flag path sending RESPAWN before replacing flags. Not a guarantee that every engine subsystem ignores the thing.

entries.description: **Renderer-written sighting latch.** C Engine/sithRender.c:3013–3024 checks bit clear and noclip off, sends SIGHTED if CAPTURED, clears AI sleeping mode for an AI with actor data, then sets the bit.
entries.caveat: Happens before the later draw call. A preset bit suppresses this block; it does not force visibility. No dedicated clearing consumer was found in the named-bit searches; generic full-field changes can still clear it. P IsThingVisible at Cog/sithCogFunctionThing.c:1448–1455 instead compares renderFrame+1 against current tick; do not equate these contracts.

entries.description: **Extra-render callback opt-in, with engine initialization writers.** C Engine/sithRender.c:3048–3052 draws base renderData, then calls the registered extra renderer if this bit is set. C Main/jkMain.c:1677–1678 registers jkPlayer_renderSaberWeaponMesh. P World/jkPlayer.c:350–440 sets it for initialized players/boss actors; :2091–2112 sets it in the JKM_DSS info-allocation helper.
entries.caveat: P callback :989–1008 needs playerInfo and puppet data; :1034–1083 branches on persuasion/Seeing, geometry, weapon model and saber flags. Bit alone neither creates weapon resources nor guarantees a visible weapon. It is not a POV-only flag. The similarly named test in current Main/jkControl.c:63 reads actorParams.flags, a different domain, and was not used as Thing.flags evidence.

entries.description: **Material/sound configuration on the supporting or struck thing.** P Engine/sithPuppet.c:647–697 selects metal footstep modes from attachedThing; P World/sithThing.c:1320–1344 selects LANDMETAL. C Gameplay/sithPlayerActions.c:141–154 selects JUMPMETAL; C Engine/sithCollision.c:1032–1044 selects HITMETAL after qualifying collision.
entries.caveat: Sound classes, attachment/marker and movement/collision conditions still apply. Metal wins before Earth in the inspected paired tests. No claim of generic damage resistance, mass, or collision strength.

entries.description: **Material/sound configuration.** Same pinned footstep/landing paths select earth modes after metal is absent; C Gameplay/sithPlayerActions.c:144–151 selects JUMPEARTH after metal.
entries.caveat: This does not change geometry, friction or physics in those paths. The inspected hit-sound branch has metal-versus-hard, not an Earth branch.

entries.description: **Unresolved.** P enum:1348; no named consumer found.
entries.caveat: Do not import Indy NOSOUND as a proven JK/MotS meaning. Literal/composite paths are not exhausted.

entries.description: **Engine-maintained water/submersion state.** P World/sithThing.c:796–807 compares underwater sector state with this bit and invokes transitions; EnterWater :822 sets it, ExitWater :882 clears it.
entries.caveat: Manually toggling the bit is not equivalent to running transition code: puppet mode, sounds, removal tests and slowdown are separate operations. C World/sithActor.c:226–248 uses it for underwater-death sound after other checks. C AI/sithAI.c:1067–1075 distinguishes observer/target water states, with a surface-physics exception; :823–844 uses it in a conditional movement path. C AI/sithAICmd.c:264–275 uses it for chosen destination height.

entries.description: **Rendering configuration bypass for one downgrade.** C Engine/sithRender.c:2946–2969: with ambient below 1, distance at/above gouradDistance and bit clear cap lighting to DIFFUSE; bit set routes to a cap at GOURAUD instead.
entries.caveat: It does not force Gouraud if desired mode is lower, nor override the earlier ambient>=1 branches. yval includes camera zoom adjustment at :2838–2843. No Main_bMotsCompat guard surrounds this consumer in the current function.

entries.description: **Destroy-on-water-entry configuration.** P World/sithThing.c:822–830 first sets WATER, then sets DESTROYED if DROWNS, optionally sending REMOVED if CAPTURED and the 0x100 gate is clear.
entries.caveat: Immediate destruction state in this path, not the player's timed breathing/drowning system. It bypasses the ordinary non-drowning splash/slowdown branch. No MotS-only guard around this bit test.

entries.description: **Destroy-on-water-exit configuration.** P World/sithThing.c:880–905 clears WATER/changes puppet mode, processes exit sound, then sets DESTROYED and conditionally sends REMOVED.
entries.caveat: Not a general swim/AI-capability flag. Its destruction branch is not prevented by bNoSplash; no MotS-only guard surrounds the bit test.

entries.description: **Splash-message opt-in.** P World/sithThing.c:831–856 entry: non-drowning/no-splash-suppression path, local player exists, this bit set, 0x100 clear; sends SPLASH to the local player's class/capture COG with entering thing as sender and source reference 1. Exit :899–920 excludes WATERCREATURE and applies suppression/local-player/0x100 conditions, using source reference 0.
entries.caveat: This is a message request, not direct creation of a splash effect. Ordinary water sound code is separate and not gated by SPLASHES. The recipient is the local player's COGs, even when another thing entered. No MotS-only guard surrounds these message tests.

entries.description: **Unresolved in bounded JK/MotS source audit.** P enum:1354; no named consumer found.
entries.caveat: Do not import Indy MOVABLE. No unused-bit guarantee; raw/composite masks and original implementations remain possible gaps.

entries.description: Original MotS stores an eligible flagged thing in one local pointer slot and skips its ordinary draw. Later eligible flagged things overwrite that slot. After normal traversal, the final stored thing is drawn once. The corresponding complete JK1.01 routine lacks this test and slot.
entries.caveat: This is not a queue for all flagged things, and it does not establish through-wall rendering. Earlier eligibility/clipping applies. The inspected JK difference is function-specific, not proof of game-wide bit nonuse. No visual runtime result is claimed.

prior_interpretation_0_1_4.description: **Current renderer's single deferred-thing slot.** C Engine/sithRender.c:2736–2737 initializes lastDrawn; :2970–2973 stores eligible thing and skips ordinary draw; :2984–2997 flushes, draws lastDrawn once, then flushes again.
prior_interpretation_0_1_4.caveat: Multiple eligible flagged things overwrite the single pointer; only the final stored thing is drawn by this deferred block. This is a conditional source consequence, not an observed rendering bug. Earlier filtering/clipping still applies (:2770–2835). “MoTS added” comments exist, but no runtime Main_bMotsCompat guard surrounds this consumer. Do not claim a general ordered queue, through-wall rendering, or retail MotS behavior.

entries.description: The inspected use is an AI event identifier and instinct event-subscription mask. AISetMode emits event 0x100 whenever its OR changes the mode word. families.title: Attachment flags
families.notes: Zero means no bits set. A raw flag write does not construct surface/thing pointers or linked lists. Use the dedicated attachment operation; 0x10 has a MotS annotation.

entries.description: The native surface attachment setter records its target and writes discriminator 1 into attach_flags. Surface attachment stores a surface; Thing-face stores a parent and face; ordinary Thing attachment maintains parent/child links and a relative position. Detach selects its surface or shared Thing/face branch from this separate field.
entries.caveat: Attachment flags are not Thing.flags: their offsets are JK +0x34 and MotS +0x3C. AttachThingToThingEx ORs its extra mask into this field after ordinary attachment. Arbitrary masks, movement propagation and complete message delivery are unproved; this does not resolve Thing 0x01000000 or attachment 0x8/0x10.

families.title: Physics flags
families.notes: Requires physics movement. Set ORs; Clear clears and lacks Set’s explicit sync request in the inspected wrapper. Template physflags= replaces the field. Bit 30 is documented from original COG use and bounded runtime evidence; its dedicated meaning and the other undeclared high bits remain unresolved.

entries.description: Gravity branch also requires nonzero mass and a sector without NOGRAVITY.

The original ApplyForce implementation sets 0x8000 while adding force divided by positive mass to a physics mover velocity, even when the supplied force vector is zero. In the inspected surface/Thing-face attached-physics block, nonzero velocity and nonzero surface drag lead to a bit test: if set, the block clears 0x8000 and skips its linear drag call.
entries.caveat: This is a conditional consumed marker, not permanent friction immunity. If those block prerequisites are not reached it is not consumed there, so a one-frame lifetime is unproved. Setting the bit alone does not apply an impulse. Other drag paths and runtime motion remain untested.

On the eligible original MotS water-entry path, the code ORs physics flags with 0x00800000, stores the result, and branches if that result is nonzero. The OR guarantees a nonzero result, so the following velocity.z *= 0.25 block is skipped whether the bit was previously clear or set. The corresponding original JK path performs that vertical-velocity multiplication and has no equivalent physics-bit OR/test there. The mapped MotS water-exit routine has no direct read or clear of this physics bit.
entries.caveat: The writer requires entry into an underwater sector, the separate Thing water-state bit previously absent, no drowning branch, the no-splash/no-notify argument zero, and physics movement. This is not a slow-once test. Broader intended meaning remains unresolved; no claim of all drag being disabled, game-wide permanent retention, or demonstrated sinking/fall-damage behavior. The current reconstruction reproduces this original branch anomaly. Runtime remains untested.

families.notes: Values4/5 remain unresolved. Mode6 has a bounded original-MotS inherited-lighting path, absent in the compared JK routines. Renderer caps and later processing still affect the result.

entries.description: In original MotS, hierarchy node flag 2 selects mesh lighting mode 6 and copies the stored lighting scalar at mesh+0x44 from the first ancestor without node flag 2. Mode 6 bypasses the ordinary mesh lighting cap and copies that scalar into every face extraLight field at face+0x30. One original producer stores the mean of computed scalar vertex-light outputs in mesh+0x44. The compared JK1.01 hierarchy/mesh routines lack this inheritance, cap exception and mode-6 copy.
entries.caveat: Scalar mode, not a flag bit. Requires a valid ancestor chain and mesh; the original walk lacks the modern null checks. Stored values can be stale, and culling, draw order, face-mode caps and later rendering still matter. It is not proof of fullbright, per-vertex RGB or a dynamic-only value. Current source instead transfers radius at this hierarchy step; original MotS parses and uses radius at mesh+0x48, distinct from the transferred +0x44. No runtime proof.

entries.description: In both original dispatchers, weapon 0x10000 selects this handler after the higher-priority 0x2000 branch. The complete handler traverses returned adjoin crossings and handles the first returned non-adjoin result. Thing hits call damage and can independently attempt force; world hits call surface impact. A non-null impact template enables a creation attempt. The final callee marks the weapon Thing.flags 0x2 for destruction.

indy_comparison.boundary: Comparison of reconstructed declarations, with selected wrapper/world consumers. No original Indy runtime or per-bit JK transfer is established.

retail_thingflags_contract.operation: Get reads DWORD at thing+0 or returns0xFFFFFFFF on null resolution. Set ORs; Clear ANDs complement; nonzero mask and nonnull resolution required. Mutators push no result and have no per-bit whitelist.
retail_thingflags_contract.sync: Conditional deferred request(thing,2); pending queue merges entries, up to16 distinct pointers. Immediate bit2 serializer copies whole flags at drain time. Transport/receive/runtime convergence untraced.
retail_thingflags_contract.method: Existing disassembly decoding checked against fresh hash-matched original PE instruction bytes; no fresh Capstone decode, execution or binary payload publication.
